core.title: Adapt only among declared valid strategies
core.given: Work involves selecting among two or more already declared valid strategies based on workload or resource signals, whether those signals are present or missing
core.when: planning, specifying, implementing or reviewing that selection
core.then: Choose only among the declared strategies via a deterministic, inspectable selection policy with a stable fallback, preserving accepted outputs and route obligations.
prefer: Use adaptive selection only where measured workload variation justifies multiple strategies and switching overhead.
Acceptance tests covering thresholds, missing metrics, fallback, oscillation and equivalence across workload classes; benchmark total cost.
Interlocking guards selecting between deterministic alternatives.
avoid: Suppressing failure behavior when signals are absent.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration (e.g. dynamic rescheduling) from this pattern; it needs new validated capabilities.
Treating this as enforcement or a new runtime dispatch option; it is advisory guidance and the stack's existing plan and source validators still apply.
core.why: Multiple strategies are only worth their switching overhead where measured workload variation justifies them, and selection must keep accepted outputs and route obligations intact.
evidence: Selection chooses only among already declared valid strategies; no undeclared route or strategy is introduced.
The selection policy (thresholds) is deterministic and inspectable, with a stable fallback, and failure behavior is not suppressed when signals are absent.
Tests and acceptance tests cover thresholds, missing metrics, fallback, oscillation and equivalence across workload classes, plus a total-cost benchmark.
Existing plan and source validators pass; no unimplemented orchestration capability is relied on.
verification: Advisory guidance for agents (severity 3, disposition advisory): not independent enforcement and not a new runtime dispatch option; the stack's existing plan and source validators still apply.
Runtime boundary: interlocking guards support deterministic alternatives; dynamic rescheduling requires new validated capabilities.

values: work selects among two or more declared strategies using workload or resource signals (including handling when those signals are absent)

fires: A plan artifact proposes choosing between already declared strategies based on measured workload size or resource availability.
An acceptance test or documentation describes how to select among declared strategies from workload or resource signals, e.g. its thresholds, fallback or behavior when those signals are missing.
Implementation or review work on an existing signal-driven selection among declared strategies.
doesNotFire: Work uses a single fixed strategy with no signal-driven selection.
Work that does not involve choosing between strategies at all.
A selection policy with thresholds or fallback that does not choose among strategies using workload or resource signals.

neutralityNotes: This advisory pattern rule is conceptual: no numbered item names a stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so bunOnly, profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty and no profile data is needed to instantiate the core. Generalizations made for neutrality: in activation.fires[0] the Bun artifact names 'wagon' and 'WMBT' became the role-level 'plan artifact'; 'acceptances' (prefer[1], evidence[2], fires[1]) became 'acceptance tests'; 'existing plan and source validators' (avoid[3], evidence[3], verifier_detail[0]) is read as the stack's existing plan-artifact and source checks, preserving the Bun deference without naming validator or finding ids; per-rule severity 3 and advisory disposition stay with the rule in core.verification. The activation facts' note fields were dropped as realization commentary; the facts, values and observability are unchanged.
